about.title: Blythe Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Blythe sits along a heavily traveled stretch of Interstate 10, where long-haul trucks, desert heat, and local traffic converge. Riverside County recorded 22 injury collisions and 28 injured people in the most recent year alone, with Wednesday evenings between 6 and 8 p.m. showing up often in the crash pattern. Whether your collision happened on I-10 Westbound, near W Hobson Way, or elsewhere in town, the aftermath can be disorienting — medical visits, missed work, and calls from an insurance adjuster asking you to explain what happened. We handle personal injury claims arising from car accidents in Blythe. Our team can review your crash, explain your options under California law, and handle communication with insurers so you're not doing it alone. There's no obligation, and no fee unless we recover something for you.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer Calls Again

items.title: California's Fault Rules Are Nuanced
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover even if you're partly blamed for the crash. We can help make sure early statements to an insurer don't unfairly shift blame onto you.

items.title: The Clock Starts Sooner Than You Think
items.desc: Most Blythe car accident claims must be filed within two years, but claims involving a government road or vehicle can require notice in as little as six months. Missing that window can end a claim before it starts.

items.title: You Never Pay Upfront
items.desc: We work on contingency, so there's no fee unless there's a recovery. That means the cost of legal help isn't a reason to delay getting answers about your crash.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally wise to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize your claim later. We can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: What if my crash happened on I-10 near Blythe but I don't know who's at fault?
items.answer: Fault isn't always obvious right after a crash on a busy corridor like I-10, especially in multi-vehicle situations. California's comparative fault rule allows recovery even if you share some responsibility. We can help gather evidence, such as crash reports and witness accounts, to sort out what happened.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim after a car accident in Blythe?
items.answer: In California, you generally have two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government entity, such as a public road authority, was involved, the notice deadline can be as short as six months. Because evidence like skid marks or traffic camera footage can disappear quickly, it helps to act promptly.
